ABSA BANKING FAUD

By: Eugene Botha | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
.........what do you do when hackers clean out your banking account the bank refuse to help you

Unique Selling Point:
A Banking scam that anyone can fall victim to

Summary:
A Large number of people have discovered that their bank accounts, or credit card accounts have been cleaned out by a hacker. When they approach the bank the bank refuses to assist and blame it on the client. They also refuse to repay the client, but when a client makes enough noise, they offer a settlement -- muck lower than the amount that was stolen. The banking ombud seems to side in 90% of cases with the banks. It seems that the problem lies mainly with ABSA. What recourse is there for victims?

Further information:
This story was passed on to me by Anna-Maria

A Large number of people have discovered that their bank accounts, or credit card accounts have been cleaned out by a hacker. When they approach the bank the bank refuses to assist and blame it on the client. They also refuse to repay the client, but when a client makes enough noise, they offer a settlement -- muck lower than the amount that was stolen. The banking ombud seems to side in 90% of cases with the banks. It seems that the problem lies mainly with ABSA. What recourse is there for victims?

This is a typical case:

My story is against ABSA bank because they aren’t helpful and blame their customer of negligence and fraud.

I am a loyal client of ABSA bank for the last 28 years.

Fraud happened on my credit card on the 31st May 2018. The bank never inform me about the monies been used from my credit card. On the 4th June, I received a sms from the bank telling me that my credit card limit + the money I put into that card is overdrawn. I then phoned the fraud department to stop my card and to find out what they mean. The fraud department then inform me that all my money is out of my account, I then asked how can it be because I didn’t use money and I did start put money R1000 into that account since February for my child’s school fees. They also then told me they do not know what is going on and asked me if I want a new card. The Friday I went and fetch my new card, and gave them my old card. The fraud department came back to me after they did an investigation and told me that I received an OTP number, I then asked the lady what is a OTP number because I didn’t even know what it stand for. The lady explained to me and I told her that I never received a number like that at any time. They also told me that the monies was used to buy some currencies so the way I understood it, it was cybercrime. They also said to me that it was my fault and negligence. I was not happy with the outcome and then took it to the dispute department and they also came back to me with the same answer that I received an OTP number what I never received it and that the monies were used to buy some currencies (Cyber currencies). I never apply for anything or know how currencies work, they also told me that this is my negligence. I asked them how can it be if I got my card with me.

After the dispute department came back I was still not happy and then took it to the ombudsman, they also told me that it is my negligence and that I received an OTP number, and they also offered to pay an amount of R2721.86 which was been used without an OTP number, I never received this money back. They also told me that I was negligence and that this is all my fault.

I am not in agreement with them of that they blame me for this. I got a debit card with them, 2 personal loans and a home loan. And in the first place why will I use the money if I paid money into that account for my child’s school fees. The bank deducted money from my debit card on a monthly basis without me giving permission and I can’t afford this, and why must I pay something I didn’t use.

I had previously also a credit card what I used that was about 6 years ago, I paid that money back.

Please can you help me with this matter because I feel that I am targeted. Please contact me on 084 603 6026.

Kind regards

Hannelie


This is typcal of what happens. Hannelie lost about R85 000. She is also one of our case studies.

But other clients lose millions, for example Mrs ME Kruger Lost more than R2 mil, and R200 000 was recovered.

She has now turned to Attorney Mark Heyink who has been fighting battles on behalf of clients against the bank and the ombus, and manages to negotiate refunds of at leat R15-20mil the last few years.

But the problem persist and Mark claims that the ombud is not effective and basically not fulfilling their mandate. He has now taken the matter to the Financial Sector Conduct Authority -- he shard all the confidential documents about that with me.

He has extensive knowledge of the law and the kind of electronic fraud that is involved, and a perfect expert for the story.

He was only back in the office on the 9th, and ran into a funeral he has to arrange. His best friend died in a car crash Tuesday. So his time is limited and he has to deal with churches and stuff he is only available on Monday as is ABSA and the Banking Ombud. Hannelie will be shot tomorrow.

Viewing Notes:
FRYING NOTES: this story is different from the SIM SWAP story where there's been investigation & arrest...EB did the story on that a few years ago.
This story is about people who suddenly discover money missing from their account -- then you approach the bank -- they make you fill in forms. The bank has an internal investigation unit that investigates.
99,9% fo the time the bank blames the client and don't refund.
People usually go to the BANK OMBUD -- they basically use the same investigation

MRS KRUGER -- 80 transactions of R25,000 -- withdrawn and deposited with CAPITEC. OBS uses the same report that comes from the bank. Approached CAPITEC & froze the account -- nobody wants to refund. DRAGGING SINCE 2016 -- she went back to the bank after the OMBUD report -- attorney for Kruger is taking it further. Mrs Kruger got 40% offer to settle, but the won't settle.

HANLIE VENTER -- R85,000 taken recently. if you make enough noise you get a partial settlement -- R2700

ATTORNEY who specialises in online fraud - MARK HEYINK -- fantastic -- he knows the scam inside out -- money goes to a syndicate...he says it's the bank's fault. VERY CRITICAL of the way in which the ombud operated.
Has represented 29 ABSA clients. R15-million in refunds recovered.

HEYINK has approached the new FSB...made representations to FSB about hos the system can be fixed. We have 2 other cases by HEYINK. All online banking fraud. With sim scam they use a simswap to get into online banking

JACO CONRADIE

also approached the OMBUD

Also ask ABSA's media person -- RIA STEYN

WG ASK:
- why is there NO alarm bell
- why is the automatic limits not helpful?

Script:


ABSA BANKING FRAUD


Voice
It’s a terrifying reality South African citizen face every day - hardcore criminals and robbers running rampant on our streets. But not all robbers come with balaclavas and guns. There is another kind, much more effective. And as their numbers grow, so do the threats they pose to us all.


Link Derek
Imagine getting an sms from your bank - your account has been cleaned out, more than R80 000 stolen overnight.


Voice
That’s exactly what happened to Hanlie Venter from Roseacre. In June last year she got a call from the bank.


Sound Up Hanlie
They said to me no, lots of money went out on the 31st of May. So, I said to them but then it’s fraud, because I didn’t use any money from the credit card.


Voice
The money was taken from her fully paid-up credit card, which she used as a savings account for her daughter.


Sound Up Hanlie
The matric farewell will be on the 19th of September. We are very excited.


Voice
But with the news from the bank prospects of a special matric farewell seem to vanish.


Sound Up Hanlie
Derek: Were you very worried at that time?

Hanlie: I was a little bit worried, but I thought it would be sorted out from the fraud department.






Voice
But her optimism turned to horror when the bank accused her of negligence and refused to refund her anything. The bank said SHE had used a One Time Pin, or OTP, to withdraw the funds.


Sound Up Hanlie
Hanlie: So, I said to her well I never received the OTP number because I didn’t even know what an OTP number is.


Voice
An OTP is a numeric code sent to customers to authorize the bank to release funds.

But Venter is adamant she never received or sent an OTP. The money simply vanished from her account.

When the bank refused a refund she turned to the Ombudsman for Banking Services, but they ruled in favour of the bank.


Link / Sound Up Hanlie

Hanlie: Somebody stole R80 000 from me, and the bank makes me feel like a criminal.

Derek: Well Hanlie Venter and her family have been through a shocking ordeal in their dispute with the bank, but they are certainly not alone.


Voice
Attorney Mark Hayink specializes in legal matters arising from online banking and has done a lot of work in the information security industry. He has been assisting a number bank clients who have been refused refunds.


Sound Up Mark
Derek: Is fraud, when it comes to online banking, becoming a bigger and bigger issue for you?

Mark: Absolutely, internet banking fraud was now 55% of the fraud that actually occurs through our banks. And the figure that they came up with was R250 000 000 is the loss suffered as a result of internet banking.


Voice
Hayink says that these figures come from data provided by the South African Banking Risk Information Centre and was recorded over a period of 8 months last year.


Sound Up Mark
Derek: Now we’ve received numerous complaints regarding Absa clients, is that your finding?

Mark: There has been predominantly the matters referred to are Absa clients, but clearly there are other banks that their clients have also been victim of these.


Voice
Reana Steyn is the current banking services ombudsman. The banking Ombud’s mandate is to investigate complaints by consumers against banks. It is a non-statutory body, funded by South African banks.


Sound Up Reana
Derek: The name of Absa seems to crop up regularly, is that your finding as well with the cases coming in here?

Reana: Yes, I think you’ll see in our annual report that last year Absa had more complaints than the other banks.


Voice
In fact, of roughly 1450 complaints relating to online banking in 2018, 684 were about ABSA, with 381 involving Capitec and 161 involving FNB. These statistics tend to differ from year to year.

Ulrich Janse van Rensburg is head of Fraud Strategy at ABSA and he says online fraud can only occur if data relating to a customers account has been compromised. This suggests negligence on the side of customers, and in such cases the banks refuse refunds.


Sound Up Ulrich
Derek: Most of the cases that we’ve come across of online fraud where clients haven’t been reimbursed or haven’t been reimbursed fully, are Absa. So how do you explain that?

Ulrich: So, as I mentioned, again, our assessment processes are robust…

Derek: I’m talking about what the ombud says, that most of the cases, recent cases let me stipulate, are Absa, you must have noticed this trend?

Ulrich: The trend is global trend, it is a global trend, so…

Derek: No, no I’m not talking about a global trend, I’m talking about here in South Africa, most of the cases where clients aren’t reimbursed or not reimbursed fully, and are put under pressure to accept offers sometimes, are with Absa. How do you explain that?

Ulrich: So, I would say most is a bit of a subjective comment, a subjective response.

Derek: This isn’t a personal view of mine Ulrich, it’s from the ombud.


Voice
In 2018, in 80% of cases, the Ombud rejected the consumers’ complaints and found in favour of the banks. This suggests that the customers are liable for the losses.


Link Derek
One of the grey areas is the question of liability, who is taking the risk when you make on-line transactions, you or the bank?


Sound Up Mark
Your terms and conditions in terms of which you agree to internet banking say that if your banking credentials are compromised, you are liable and responsible.


Voice
That means that the bank will hold you responsible, even if you unknowingly fall victim to fraud. It happened to this woman, who we’ll call Summer. She’s been an Absa client for decades, and has asked us to hide her identity because she is fearful that her relationship with ABSA could be compromised.


Sound Up “Summer”
Summer: My cellphone was off for a few days, and I thought it was lack of signal, but when I realized it wasn’t, I went to the Vodacom shop and asked them to check it out and investigate. And that’s when they told me my sim card was swopped and my contract was cancelled.


Voice
On advice from the shop assistant, she rushed to the bank, only to find that her credit card had been maxed out to the tune of nearly R90 000. The hackers had also applied on her behalf for a personal loan that was approved, but not yet paid out.

___________________________________________________________________

Sound Up Summer:
Summer: well, I was so shocked. Because how could ABSA allow all these things? When they know… I mean, how could they allow it?

Voice:
But she was in for a bigger shock - the bank refused to accept any liability.

Sound Up “Summer”

Summer: My money disappeared from my banking account, and Absa accused me of negligence, and basically saying I stole my own money.


Voice
This man, whom we’ll call Winter, also fell victim a fraudulent sim swap and lost more than half a million rand.


Sound Up “Winter”
Derek: What was the attitude of the bank, was there no acceptance that this was fraud, which you hadn’t perpetrated?

Winter: Yes they said it was fraud, but they wash their hands of it. It was very traumatic. One had to incur medical costs because one became really depressed. It is a terrible shock and one starts to think weird thoughts about what to do.


Sound Up “Summer”

I really felt so betrayed by my own bank.


Voice
In another case hackers transferred R2,2 mil in 85 transaction from a client’s account. She declined to appear on camera and the bank has so far refused to refund her anything.


Sound Up Ulrich
Derek: clients, sometimes elderly, who’ve lost tens if not hundreds of thousands of Rand. And you haven’t been willing to compensate them fully?

Ulrich: Based on the merit of those cases, on an individual basis, we have assessed all the facts. We have also what we refer to in our robust assessment process, a system audit trail. The system audit trail tracks all the activity on the customer’s profile.

Derek: Look it may be robust but it’s not compassionate.


Voice
In some cases, the bank does offer reimbursement, in Summer and Winter’s cases Absa offered 50%. However, Hanlie was only offered R5000 of the more than R80 000 that was stolen.


Sound Up Ulrich
In certain cases where we see that to an extent we could have recovered some of the funds, in other words yes the customer was at fault, and let’s say he lost a R100 000, and we believe there is a certain amount of the R100 000 that within reasonable time we could have recovered, we would honour that obligation and respond and refund those customers.


Voice
However, the refund is then accompanied by a non-disclosure agreement.

Sound Up Ulrich
Derek: Why do you gag your clients, tell them not to speak to the media, and we’ve had to interview a couple of them with their identity hidden. Like they are criminals.

Ulrich: If it’s considered a gag, that’s harsh. In cases where we provide the customer an offer letter of a refund, or a reimbursement as we call it, we ask the customer not to disclose the information. Because the customer does not have all the facts and the customer is not necessarily au fait with all the content on the decision that’s been made.

Derek: A number of your clients say that they were left feeling like the criminals themselves?

Ulrich: If customers feel that it’s not sufficient, and they don’t understand how it occurred, then we need to get closer to those customers and unpack it…

Derek: You need to get closer to them, but I’m saying they didn’t feel close to you at all, and they felt like criminals, that’s what I’m telling you.

Ulrich: Ok, I can tell you now the last thing we want to do is treat our customers like aliens, or criminals in this case.


Voice
In many instances the consumer is hampered by a lack of understanding of the terms and conditions they have to sign up to when they enrol for online banking services.
A 2018 diagnostic report by the World Bank about South African banks found that some of the stipulations about risk and liability where online banking is involved, is could be deemed unfair to consumers. This report states:

“Several banks’ terms and conditions contain broad exclusions from liability in relation to matters including their processes, systems, or data breaches… Such an exclusion shifts more of the risk onto the customer in circumstances where he or she would be significantly less well placed to mitigate it.”

A further problem is that in reaching its conclusions, the banking Ombudsman only examines the two versions of events submitted by the complainant and bank and does not investigate or call expert witnesses.
So, if both bank and ombudsman rule against a consumer, their only recourse would be taking the bank to court.


Link Court
One aspect that complicates the matter is that there hasn’t been a court case between a bank and a client, to legally determine where the liability should fall.


Voice
This means that there are no clear legal guidelines to establish how liability should be determined in complex online banking fraud cases.


Sound Up Ombud
Once we have our first case, and there’s case law, when there is precedent, we can follow that. We haven’t had a single case in this country. And of course, our body, which is an alternative dispute resolution, we’re the alternative to the court, is not the right place to set a precedent.


Voice
A future court case may bring clarity about liability in cases of online banking, but the fact remains that online banking comes with some risk.

Sound Up Hanlie
and at the end of the day, somebody stole R80 000 from me… (4)

And then, to add insult to injury, your bank accuses you of negligence and refuses to reimburse you the stolen funds. (8)

Sound Up Hanlie
and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (4)

Sound Up Hanlie
somebody stole R80 000 from me, and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (7)




2nd Promo 15 sec

Voice
We meet online banking users who have had their accounts cleaned out by online criminal syndicates and ask whether our banks are doing enough to protect their customers. (9)


Sound Up Hanlie
and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (4)




Promo 10 sec

Voice
On line banking fraud is increasing year on year at an alarming rate and losses are running into the hundreds of millions of rands. But who is liable for the losses, you or the bank? (10)

But not all robbers come with balaclavas and guns. There is another kind, much more effective. And as their numbers grow, so do the threats they pose to us all. Link Derek Imagine getting an sms from your bank - your account has been cleaned out, more than R80 000 stolen overnight. Voice That’s exactly what happened to Hanlie Venter from Roseacre. In June last year she got a call from the bank. Sound Up Hanlie They said to me no, lots of money went out on the 31st of May. So, I said to them but then it’s fraud, because I didn’t use any money from the credit card. Voice The money was taken from her fully paid-up credit card, which she used as a savings account for her daughter. Sound Up Hanlie The matric farewell will be on the 19th of September. We are very excited. Voice But with the news from the bank prospects of a special matric farewell seem to vanish. Sound Up Hanlie Derek: Were you very worried at that time? Hanlie: I was a little bit worried, but I thought it would be sorted out from the fraud department. Voice But her optimism turned to horror when the bank accused her of negligence and refused to refund her anything. The bank said SHE had used a One Time Pin, or OTP, to withdraw the funds. Sound Up Hanlie Hanlie: So, I said to her well I never received the OTP number because I didn’t even know what an OTP number is. Voice An OTP is a numeric code sent to customers to authorize the bank to release funds. But Venter is adamant she never received or sent an OTP. The money simply vanished from her account. When the bank refused a refund she turned to the Ombudsman for Banking Services, but they ruled in favour of the bank. Link / Sound Up Hanlie Hanlie: Somebody stole R80 000 from me, and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. Derek: Well Hanlie Venter and her family have been through a shocking ordeal in their dispute with the bank, but they are certainly not alone. Voice Attorney Mark Hayink specializes in legal matters arising from online banking and has done a lot of work in the information security industry. He has been assisting a number bank clients who have been refused refunds. Sound Up Mark Derek: Is fraud, when it comes to online banking, becoming a bigger and bigger issue for you? Mark: Absolutely, internet banking fraud was now 55% of the fraud that actually occurs through our banks. And the figure that they came up with was R250 000 000 is the loss suffered as a result of internet banking. Voice Hayink says that these figures come from data provided by the South African Banking Risk Information Centre and was recorded over a period of 8 months last year. Sound Up Mark Derek: Now we’ve received numerous complaints regarding Absa clients, is that your finding? Mark: There has been predominantly the matters referred to are Absa clients, but clearly there are other banks that their clients have also been victim of these. Voice Reana Steyn is the current banking services ombudsman. The banking Ombud’s mandate is to investigate complaints by consumers against banks. It is a non-statutory body, funded by South African banks. Sound Up Reana Derek: The name of Absa seems to crop up regularly, is that your finding as well with the cases coming in here? Reana: Yes, I think you’ll see in our annual report that last year Absa had more complaints than the other banks. Voice In fact, of roughly 1450 complaints relating to online banking in 2018, 684 were about ABSA, with 381 involving Capitec and 161 involving FNB. These statistics tend to differ from year to year. Ulrich Janse van Rensburg is head of Fraud Strategy at ABSA and he says online fraud can only occur if data relating to a customers account has been compromised. This suggests negligence on the side of customers, and in such cases the banks refuse refunds. Sound Up Ulrich Derek: Most of the cases that we’ve come across of online fraud where clients haven’t been reimbursed or haven’t been reimbursed fully, are Absa. So how do you explain that? Ulrich: So, as I mentioned, again, our assessment processes are robust… Derek: I’m talking about what the ombud says, that most of the cases, recent cases let me stipulate, are Absa, you must have noticed this trend? Ulrich: The trend is global trend, it is a global trend, so… Derek: No, no I’m not talking about a global trend, I’m talking about here in South Africa, most of the cases where clients aren’t reimbursed or not reimbursed fully, and are put under pressure to accept offers sometimes, are with Absa. How do you explain that? Ulrich: So, I would say most is a bit of a subjective comment, a subjective response. Derek: This isn’t a personal view of mine Ulrich, it’s from the ombud. Voice In 2018, in 80% of cases, the Ombud rejected the consumers’ complaints and found in favour of the banks. This suggests that the customers are liable for the losses. Link Derek One of the grey areas is the question of liability, who is taking the risk when you make on-line transactions, you or the bank? Sound Up Mark Your terms and conditions in terms of which you agree to internet banking say that if your banking credentials are compromised, you are liable and responsible. Voice That means that the bank will hold you responsible, even if you unknowingly fall victim to fraud. It happened to this woman, who we’ll call Summer. She’s been an Absa client for decades, and has asked us to hide her identity because she is fearful that her relationship with ABSA could be compromised. Sound Up “Summer” Summer: My cellphone was off for a few days, and I thought it was lack of signal, but when I realized it wasn’t, I went to the Vodacom shop and asked them to check it out and investigate. And that’s when they told me my sim card was swopped and my contract was cancelled. Voice On advice from the shop assistant, she rushed to the bank, only to find that her credit card had been maxed out to the tune of nearly R90 000. The hackers had also applied on her behalf for a personal loan that was approved, but not yet paid out. ___________________________________________________________________ Sound Up Summer: Summer: well, I was so shocked. Because how could ABSA allow all these things? When they know… I mean, how could they allow it? Voice: But she was in for a bigger shock - the bank refused to accept any liability. Sound Up “Summer” Summer: My money disappeared from my banking account, and Absa accused me of negligence, and basically saying I stole my own money. Voice This man, whom we’ll call Winter, also fell victim a fraudulent sim swap and lost more than half a million rand. Sound Up “Winter” Derek: What was the attitude of the bank, was there no acceptance that this was fraud, which you hadn’t perpetrated? Winter: Yes they said it was fraud, but they wash their hands of it. It was very traumatic. One had to incur medical costs because one became really depressed. It is a terrible shock and one starts to think weird thoughts about what to do. Sound Up “Summer” I really felt so betrayed by my own bank. Voice In another case hackers transferred R2,2 mil in 85 transaction from a client’s account. She declined to appear on camera and the bank has so far refused to refund her anything. Sound Up Ulrich Derek: clients, sometimes elderly, who’ve lost tens if not hundreds of thousands of Rand. And you haven’t been willing to compensate them fully? Ulrich: Based on the merit of those cases, on an individual basis, we have assessed all the facts. We have also what we refer to in our robust assessment process, a system audit trail. The system audit trail tracks all the activity on the customer’s profile. Derek: Look it may be robust but it’s not compassionate. Voice In some cases, the bank does offer reimbursement, in Summer and Winter’s cases Absa offered 50%. However, Hanlie was only offered R5000 of the more than R80 000 that was stolen. Sound Up Ulrich In certain cases where we see that to an extent we could have recovered some of the funds, in other words yes the customer was at fault, and let’s say he lost a R100 000, and we believe there is a certain amount of the R100 000 that within reasonable time we could have recovered, we would honour that obligation and respond and refund those customers. Voice However, the refund is then accompanied by a non-disclosure agreement. Sound Up Ulrich Derek: Why do you gag your clients, tell them not to speak to the media, and we’ve had to interview a couple of them with their identity hidden. Like they are criminals. Ulrich: If it’s considered a gag, that’s harsh. In cases where we provide the customer an offer letter of a refund, or a reimbursement as we call it, we ask the customer not to disclose the information. Because the customer does not have all the facts and the customer is not necessarily au fait with all the content on the decision that’s been made. Derek: A number of your clients say that they were left feeling like the criminals themselves? Ulrich: If customers feel that it’s not sufficient, and they don’t understand how it occurred, then we need to get closer to those customers and unpack it… Derek: You need to get closer to them, but I’m saying they didn’t feel close to you at all, and they felt like criminals, that’s what I’m telling you. Ulrich: Ok, I can tell you now the last thing we want to do is treat our customers like aliens, or criminals in this case. Voice In many instances the consumer is hampered by a lack of understanding of the terms and conditions they have to sign up to when they enrol for online banking services. A 2018 diagnostic report by the World Bank about South African banks found that some of the stipulations about risk and liability where online banking is involved, is could be deemed unfair to consumers. This report states: “Several banks’ terms and conditions contain broad exclusions from liability in relation to matters including their processes, systems, or data breaches… Such an exclusion shifts more of the risk onto the customer in circumstances where he or she would be significantly less well placed to mitigate it.” A further problem is that in reaching its conclusions, the banking Ombudsman only examines the two versions of events submitted by the complainant and bank and does not investigate or call expert witnesses. So, if both bank and ombudsman rule against a consumer, their only recourse would be taking the bank to court. Link Court One aspect that complicates the matter is that there hasn’t been a court case between a bank and a client, to legally determine where the liability should fall. Voice This means that there are no clear legal guidelines to establish how liability should be determined in complex online banking fraud cases. Sound Up Ombud Once we have our first case, and there’s case law, when there is precedent, we can follow that. We haven’t had a single case in this country. And of course, our body, which is an alternative dispute resolution, we’re the alternative to the court, is not the right place to set a precedent. Voice A future court case may bring clarity about liability in cases of online banking, but the fact remains that online banking comes with some risk. (9) Sound Up Hanlie and at the end of the day, somebody stole R80 000 from me… (4) Voice And then, to add insult to injury, your bank accuses you of negligence and refuses to reimburse you the stolen funds. (8) Sound Up Hanlie and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (4) Sound Up “Summer” I really felt so betrayed by my own bank. (4) 1st Promo 15 sec Voice Imagine having your bank account cleaned out by online hackers through no fault of your own, only to discover that your bank won’t refund your losses. (8) Sound Up Hanlie somebody stole R80 000 from me, and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (7) 2nd Promo 15 sec Voice We meet online banking users who have had their accounts cleaned out by online criminal syndicates and ask whether our banks are doing enough to protect their customers. (9) Sound Up Hanlie and the bank makes me feel like a criminal. (4) Promo 10 sec Voice On line banking fraud is increasing year on year at an alarming rate and losses are running into the hundreds of millions of rands. But who is liable for the losses, you or the bank? (10)

metadata.Summary: A Large number of people have discovered that their bank accounts, or credit card accounts have been cleaned out by a hacker. When they approach the bank the bank refuses to assist and blame it on the client. They also refuse to repay the client, but when a client makes enough noise, they offer a settlement -- muck lower than the amount that was stolen. The banking ombud seems to side in 90% of cases with the banks. It seems that the problem lies mainly with ABSA. What recourse is there for victims?
metadata.Further information: This story was passed on to me by Anna-Maria A Large number of people have discovered that their bank accounts, or credit card accounts have been cleaned out by a hacker. When they approach the bank the bank refuses to assist and blame it on the client. They also refuse to repay the client, but when a client makes enough noise, they offer a settlement -- muck lower than the amount that was stolen. The banking ombud seems to side in 90% of cases with the banks. It seems that the problem lies mainly with ABSA. What recourse is there for victims? This is a typical case: My story is against ABSA bank because they aren’t helpful and blame their customer of negligence and fraud. I am a loyal client of ABSA bank for the last 28 years. Fraud happened on my credit card on the 31st May 2018. The bank never inform me about the monies been used from my credit card. On the 4th June, I received a sms from the bank telling me that my credit card limit + the money I put into that card is overdrawn. I then phoned the fraud department to stop my card and to find out what they mean. The fraud department then inform me that all my money is out of my account, I then asked how can it be because I didn’t use money and I did start put money R1000 into that account since February for my child’s school fees. They also then told me they do not know what is going on and asked me if I want a new card. The Friday I went and fetch my new card, and gave them my old card. The fraud department came back to me after they did an investigation and told me that I received an OTP number, I then asked the lady what is a OTP number because I didn’t even know what it stand for. The lady explained to me and I told her that I never received a number like that at any time. They also told me that the monies was used to buy some currencies so the way I understood it, it was cybercrime. They also said to me that it was my fault and negligence. I was not happy with the outcome and then took it to the dispute department and they also came back to me with the same answer that I received an OTP number what I never received it and that the monies were used to buy some currencies (Cyber currencies). I never apply for anything or know how currencies work, they also told me that this is my negligence. I asked them how can it be if I got my card with me. After the dispute department came back I was still not happy and then took it to the ombudsman, they also told me that it is my negligence and that I received an OTP number, and they also offered to pay an amount of R2721.86 which was been used without an OTP number, I never received this money back. They also told me that I was negligence and that this is all my fault. I am not in agreement with them of that they blame me for this. I got a debit card with them, 2 personal loans and a home loan. And in the first place why will I use the money if I paid money into that account for my child’s school fees. The bank deducted money from my debit card on a monthly basis without me giving permission and I can’t afford this, and why must I pay something I didn’t use. I had previously also a credit card what I used that was about 6 years ago, I paid that money back. Please can you help me with this matter because I feel that I am targeted. Please contact me on 084 603 6026. Kind regards Hannelie This is typcal of what happens. Hannelie lost about R85 000. She is also one of our case studies. But other clients lose millions, for example Mrs ME Kruger Lost more than R2 mil, and R200 000 was recovered. She has now turned to Attorney Mark Heyink who has been fighting battles on behalf of clients against the bank and the ombus, and manages to negotiate refunds of at leat R15-20mil the last few years. But the problem persist and Mark claims that the ombud is not effective and basically not fulfilling their mandate. He has now taken the matter to the Financial Sector Conduct Authority -- he shard all the confidential documents about that with me. He has extensive knowledge of the law and the kind of electronic fraud that is involved, and a perfect expert for the story. He was only back in the office on the 9th, and ran into a funeral he has to arrange. His best friend died in a car crash Tuesday. So his time is limited and he has to deal with churches and stuff he is only available on Monday as is ABSA and the Banking Ombud. Hannelie will be shot tomorrow. The bank has an internal investigation unit that investigates. 99,9% fo the time the bank blames the client and don't refund. People usually go to the BANK OMBUD -- they basically use the same investigation MRS KRUGER -- 80 transactions of R25,000 -- withdrawn and deposited with CAPITEC. OBS uses the same report that comes from the bank. Approached CAPITEC & froze the account -- nobody wants to refund. DRAGGING SINCE 2016 -- she went back to the bank after the OMBUD report -- attorney for Kruger is taking it further. Mrs Kruger got 40% offer to settle, but the won't settle. VERY CRITICAL of the way in which the ombud operated. Has represented 29 ABSA clients. R15-million in refunds recovered.
